content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse structure: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamoyl amide) attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the fragment: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 is a sulfonamide linking phenyl ring (sulfonyl phenyl) to an aniline with unsaturated amide.

Goal: 3 steps retrosynthesis.

We have guidance: step 1: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide. In retrosynthesis, we break amide to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step 2: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with decarboxylation). So forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. In retrosynthesis, we break the C=C and carboxylate to give aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give amine and sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl acid? but typical is sulfonyl chloride). So we can propose sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) and aniline.

Thus propose route:

Target (T) = methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to phenyl with α,β-unsaturated amide attached to aniline.

Retrosynthetic disconnections:

1) Break amide C(=O)-N linking the cinnamoyl amide to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursors: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Wait the amide is between the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl and an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So product after disconnection: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (C=CC(=O)OH) attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Actually the carbonyl is attached to the phenyl sulfonyl phenyl? Let's examine: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2) has a substituent /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the carbonyl is attached to the phenyl ring via the α,β-unsaturated chain: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline. So the amide carbonyl is attached to the α,β-unsaturated chain, not to the sulfonyl phenyl. So after breaking amide, we get the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to phenyl sulfonyl phenyl? Actually the acid would be phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (cinnamic acid) attached to the phenyl sulfonyl phenyl? Wait the phenyl sulfonyl phenyl is the same phenyl ring (c2) that bears the side chain. So the acid would be the same phenyl ring with side chain: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH. So the precursor is that phenyl ring with unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) attached, plus aniline (c3ccccc3N) as amine.

Thus step 1: amide formation between cinnamic acid (attached to phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl) and aniline (para-aminophenyl?). Actually aniline is unsubstituted phenyl with an NH2 (c3ccccc3N). So we need aniline as nucleophile.

Step 2: The cinnamic acid can be derived via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (the same phenyl ring with sulfonamide) and malonic acid. The aldehyde would be the phenyl ring bearing sulfonamide and a CHO group (instead of CH=CH-COOH). So we need to generate the aldehyde: phenyl-CHO attached to sulfonamide phenyl.

Thus step 2: aldehyde + malonic acid -> cinnamic acid (with decarboxylation). So we need aldehyde precursor: the phenyl ring bearing sulfonamide and CHO.

Step 3: The sulfonamide can be formed from amine (the phenyl ring with methyl group) and sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl). The amine is p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline). The sulfonyl chloride is p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl group attached to the phenyl ring (c2) is sulfonyl attached to the first phenyl (c1) which has methyl. The sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (CH3C6H4SO2Cl). The amine is the other phenyl (c2) which is also p-substituted? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (c1) which has methyl. So the amine is p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline). The sulfonyl chloride is the sulfonyl attached to the second phenyl (c2) which is unsubstituted phenyl (but later has side chain). So the sulfonyl chloride is 4-(...?) Actually the sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl (c2) which later bears the cinnamic acid side chain. So we need to generate sulfonyl chloride from that phenyl ring (c2) with appropriate substituents (maybe after step 2 we have aldehyde on that ring; we can convert aldehyde to sulfonyl chloride? Not typical. Better: we can form sulfonamide first, then do Doebner on the phenyl ring bearing sulfonamide? The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl; the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl. So we can start with p-toluidine (first phenyl) and p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (second phenyl). But the second phenyl later gets transformed to aldehyde then cinnamic acid then amide. So we need to have sulfonyl chloride that already has the aldehyde substituent? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring that will later be functionalized at para position with the side chain. The sulfonyl chloride could be p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (para-methyl). But after sulfonamide formation, the phenyl ring (c2) will have a methyl group at para? In target, the second phenyl (c2) does not have methyl; it has the side chain at para position relative to sulfonyl group? Let's examine SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

First phenyl: c1 with methyl (C) at position 1, and NSO2 attached at para (position 4). So first phenyl is p-tolyl with sulfonamide.

Second phenyl: c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to sulfonyl group at position 1 (sulfonyl attached to N). It has side chain at para position (relative to sulfonyl). No other substituents.

Thus sulfonyl chloride needed is p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? No, the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl, which is unsubstituted phenyl (no methyl). So the sulfonyl chloride is benzenesulfonyl chloride (PhSO2Cl). After sulfonamide formation, we have PhSO2-NH-Ph-CH3 (p-toluidine). Then we need to functionalize the phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl (the PhSO2 part) at para position to introduce the cinnamic acid side chain. That can be done after sulfonamide formation via Doebner modification on that phenyl ring (which now has sulfonamide attached). So step 2: aromatic aldehyde (para-formyl phenyl sulfonamide) + malonic acid -> cinnamic acid attached to phenyl sulfonamide. So the aldehyde is 4-formylbenzenesulfonamide (i.e., sulfonamide phenyl with CHO para). That can be obtained from sulfonamide (product of step 3) via formylation (e.g., Vilsmeier). But we are limited to 3 steps; we need to incorporate aldehyde formation maybe as part of step 3? However the guidance only includes sulfonamide formation, Doebner modification, amide coupling. So we can assume aldehyde is available as starting material (maybe commercially). So step 3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and benzenesulfonyl chloride gives sulfonamide (p-tolyl-NH-SO2-Ph). This sulfonamide is a starting material for step 2 (Doebner) where we need aldehyde (para-formyl) on the phenyl attached to sulfonyl. But our sulfonamide product does not have aldehyde. So we need aldehyde as separate starting material; but we only have 3 steps total. Perhaps we can reverse order: first Doebner modification on a phenyl aldehyde (para-formyl benzenesulfonyl chloride?) Not typical.

Alternative: Use Doebner modification on a phenyl aldehyde that already contains sulfonyl chloride? Could we have aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride group? That would be 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CHO). Then Doebner gives cinnamic acid sulfonyl chloride, then amide coupling with aniline, then sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine? That would be 3 steps: 1) Doebner: aldehyde (4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated sulfonyl chloride (cinnamic sulfonyl chloride). 2) Amide coupling: that acid (cinnamic sulfonyl chloride? Wait it's sulfonyl chloride not acid) Actually Doebner yields α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid, not sulfonyl chloride. So we need aldehyde that is sulfonyl chloride? The sulfonyl chloride is not part of the aldehyde; the aldehyde is just aromatic aldehyde. The sulfonyl chloride is separate. So we cannot combine.

Thus maybe the route: 1) Sulfonamide formation (p-toluidine + benzenesulfonyl chloride) -> sulfonamide intermediate (compound A). 2) Doebner modification on compound A after formylation? But we don't have formylation step. However maybe the sulfonamide intermediate already has an aldehyde at para position (if we start from p-toluidine and 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride). That is, we can use 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl attached to phenyl with CHO para). Then sulfonamide formation yields sulfonamide with aldehyde already present. Then Doebner modification on that aldehyde gives cinnamic acid attached to sulfonamide. Then amide coupling with aniline gives final product. That is 3 steps: (i) sulfonamide formation using 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride and p-toluidine; (ii) Doebner modification of the aldehyde (on the sulfonamide) with malonic acid to give α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid) attached to sulfonamide; (iii) amide coupling of that acid with aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give final product.

Thus we need templates for sulfonamide formation (breaking sulfonamide to amine + sulfonyl chloride). We have template ID 733 (from earlier search) for sulfonamide formation. Good.

Doebner modification template: we need a template that breaks α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. Search for functional groups broken: "C-C double bonds" and formed: "aldehydes"? Actually Doebner forms double bond, breaks C-C and C-O. In retrosynthesis, we break double bond and carboxylic acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. So we need a template where product is α,β-unsaturated acid, reactants are aldehyde + malonic acid. Let's search for functional groups broken: "C-C double bonds" maybe. Also "carboxylic acid" broken? The forward reaction forms acid, so broken in retro is acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid + CO2. So in retro, we break the double bond and the acid to give aldehyde + malonic acid. So functional groups broken: "C-C double bonds" and "carboxylic acid"? The product has carboxylic acid; broken in retro means we remove it. So we can search for templates with functional_groups_broken ["C-C double bonds", "carboxylic acid"] and formed ["aldehydes"]? Not sure.

Let's search for templates with functional_groups_formed ["aldehydes"] and broken ["C-C double bonds"] maybe.
